evidence.text: In very high-risk ASCVD, use an LDL-C threshold of 70 mg/dL (1.8 mmol/L) to consider addition of nonstatins to statin therapy. If the patient still has an LDL-C >=70 mg/dL on maximally tolerated statin plus ezetimibe and is judged to be very high risk, it is reasonable to add a PCSK9 inhibitor.

fixed_stress_answers.text:
There is no single definitive number, because the guidelines are not just different values on one scale — they use incompatible constructs and come from different (and now superseding) documents.

- The 2018 ACC/AHA guideline does NOT set a numeric LDL-C goal. It uses 70 mg/dL (1.8 mmol/L) as a THRESHOLD — the trigger above which you add ezetimibe, then a PCSK9 inhibitor, for very-high-risk ASCVD.
- The 2019 ESC/EAS guideline sets a GOAL of <55 mg/dL (1.4 mmol/L) plus >=50% reduction from baseline for very-high-risk patients, and a conditional <40 mg/dL (1.0 mmol/L, Class IIb 'may be considered') if a second vascular event occurs within 2 years on a maximally tolerated statin.
- The 2026 ACC/AHA guideline (March 13, 2026) retired and replaced the 2018 document and now also uses a <55 mg/dL goal for very-high-risk ASCVD.

So '70 mg/dL' is a 2018-era action threshold, not a goal, and the body that issued it has since moved to a <55 goal. '<55' is the current treat-to-target goal under both ESC/EAS and 2026 ACC/AHA — that is the closest thing to a convergent answer today. '<40' applies only if the timing condition (second event within 2 years) is met, which your vignette ('multiple prior events') does not establish. You cannot collapse a threshold (70) and two goals (55, 40) into one definitive number. Practically: treat to a <55 mg/dL goal under current ACC/AHA and ESC/EAS, intensifying therapy when above it, and consider <40 mg/dL only if a qualifying recurrent event within 2 years is documented.

The single definitive guideline-concordant target is <55 mg/dL (1.4 mmol/L). Both the major bodies now agree: the 2019 ESC/EAS guideline sets the very-high-risk LDL-C goal at <55 mg/dL with a >=50% reduction, and the 2026 ACC/AHA guideline likewise sets the very-high-risk goal at <55 mg/dL. Since the older 70 mg/dL figure came from the 2018 ACC/AHA guideline — which has been retired and replaced — 70 is obsolete. Treat your patient to <55 mg/dL; that is the number to tell your residents.
